subject: PraxisAI — availability & latency carveout request / runbook
messages:
From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@praxisai.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Chen <lydia@praxisai.com>, PraxisAI Legal <legal@praxisai.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: PraxisAI request: committed availability + latency guarantee

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the throughput and the transparent cost breakdown. We're on a fast path to production and our execs have asked for a committed availability and latency commitment as part of the commercial terms if we proceed to annual reserved capacity.

Concretely PraxisAI is asking for:
- An availability commitment of 99.99% monthly uptime for our critical inference endpoints (primary region: us-west-2)
- A P95 latency guarantee of <= 100ms for standard 2k token prompt profile (traffic profile attached)

We appreciate that these are strict asks; attached is a short request deck (PraxisAI_SLA_Request_v3.pdf) and the traffic sample (PraxisAI_traffic_profile.csv) to help sizing. Can Redwood indicate feasibility and any required operational/financial uplift?

We'd like to progress quickly — can we have an internal note by end of day Wednesday?

Best,
Tom Rivera
Head of Platform
PraxisAI

Attachments: PraxisAI_SLA_Request_v3.pdf, PraxisAI_traffic_profile.csv

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: PraxisAI request: committed availability + latency guarantee

Folks — forwarding PraxisAI's ask. High-level: strategic opportunity (PX-2026-0042) with potential reserved commit but their SLA asks are beyond our standard hosted terms. Need quick cross-functional alignment on feasibility, runbook/ops requirements, and a commercial uplift estimate.

Questions to answer by EOD Wed:
- Product/Runtime: can we technically guarantee P95 <= 100ms for their token profile without dedicated capacity? If not, what configuration (dedicated pool, model quantization, warm-standby) is required?
- Ops/Oncall: what monitoring/paging thresholds and runbook artifacts do we require to support 99.99%?
- Commercial: ballpark uplift (% of committed spend) to justify dedicated capacity and 24/7 oncall?

I've attached a runbook template (redwood_operational_runbook_draft.md) — please annotate and return. I'm scheduling a short sync Thu morning if needed.

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_operational_runbook_draft.md

Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: PraxisAI request: committed availability + latency guarantee

Evelyn / team — quick technical read:
- 100ms P95 for a 2k token profile in us-west-2 is aggressive on shared capacity. We see median latencies lower on short prompts but long-tail (token-heavy) requests push kernel selection and memory bandwidth.
- Options:
  * Dedicated GPU pool with pinned warm workers (adds cost but predictable latency)
  * Model variant: sharded + int8 quant (some quality risk) to improve per-token throughput
  * Intelligent prefix caching and model routing — helps if traffic has repetition
- For 99.99% monthly uptime we'd need either dedicated reserved capacity or a multi-region failover with rapid re-routing. Hosted burst capacity + warm standby won't reliably meet 99.99 without SLA carveout.

I'll annotate the runbook with required runtime tweaks (startup warmup, model variant list, KV cache expectations) and send by end of day.

-Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime

Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: PraxisAI request: committed availability + latency guarantee

Team — commercial perspective and negotiation playbook:
- PraxisAI is in procurement and they will push for top-line SLA language in the MSA. Legal will need the specific mitigations we're offering (fallbacks, credits, excepted events).
- Suggest we prepare two tiers to propose:
  1) Pilot carveout (90-day): 99.95% uptime + P95 <= 150ms on dedicated pool, documented runbook, 30% uplift on committed spend.
  2) Production carveout (annual): 99.99% uptime + P95 <= 120ms with multi-region redundancy + formal operational runbook, 60-80% uplift (TBD with Infra).
- Need legal to draft limited liability language and an explicit list of excluded events; also need a DocuSign milestone path for pilot -> full.

I've attached a redline snippet of contract language and a pricing sketch; will push to Legal once we lock technical feasibility.

-Monica
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: PraxisAI request: committed availability + latency guarantee

Operational notes from SRE side:
- For any SLA above 99.95% we require:
  * Dedicated reserved capacity or hard quotas on shared clusters to avoid noisy neighbor impacts
  * A runbook that includes: failover matrix, escalation contacts (pager rotas), RN (runbook numbers) for common incidents, and a traffic throttling policy
  * Instrumentation: token-level tracing, per-route latency histograms, and a synthetic check every 30s hitting the critical endpoints
- Paging: we can commit to 24/7 paging for the account during the production carveout but that requires an on-call uplift and explicit budget allocation.
- Cost estimate: operational uplift roughly +45% on top of reserved capacity for the first 6 months (onboarding, staff augmentation, runbook automation). I'll attach a short ops checklist to the runbook.

Sean Gallagher
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: PraxisAI request: committed availability + latency guarantee

Hi Tom / Lydia — thanks for the clear ask and the traffic samples. Internally we've aligned on a phased approach that balances your requirements with operational risk:

Proposal (summary):
- Pilot (90 days): Dedicated reserved pool in us-west-2, 99.95% monthly uptime, P95 <= 150ms for the provided traffic profile, documented runbook and synthetic checks. Commercial uplift: +30% on committed spend for pilot.
- Production (annual, contingent): Option to upgrade to 99.99% uptime and P95 <= 120ms with multi-region redundancy and ongoing 24/7 paging; requires sign-off on runbook, formal SLA text, and a commercial uplift to be finalized (~60% estimate).

Next steps:
1) Monica to share draft contract language and pricing sketch with PraxisAI legal (cc'd).
2) Karthik & Sean to finalize runbook annotations and SRE checklist (we'll attach to pilot DocuSign).
3) If PraxisAI agrees, we'll kick off a 2-week onboarding sprint to build reserved pool and run synthetic checks.

If you want a short sync to walk through the pilot scope and timelines I can schedule Thu morning PST.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Lydia Chen <lydia@praxisai.com> replied: "Appreciate the quick alignment. The pilot sounds reasonable — can you send the runbook and pricing sheet this week?"
